extracted.intended_audience: NLP / ML researchers and practitioners working on humor generation and evaluation for large language models
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluation criteria for producing and assessing humorous outputs from LLMs using a persona-based Mixture-of-Thought (MoT) distillation pipeline, supervised fine-tuning, and preference-alignment experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cognitive Synergy Framework (persona-based MoT distillation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operationalize psychological humor theories into multiple cognitive personas and adapt the Mixture-of-Thought (MoT) paradigm to model divergent thinking for humor generation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instantiate distinct cognitive personas as latent experts within a MoT ensemble to route generation into low-probability, high-variance regions of semantic space where humor occurs. Use the ensemble to synthesize a diverse, theoretically grounded corpus of synthetic data for student model distillation. (Paper contribution: 'We introduce the Cognitive Synergy Framework, a methodology for generating diverse, high-quality humor data by deploying specialized psychological personas as latent experts.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Design explicit Cognitive Personas mapped to humor theories
rubrics_metrics.description: Define a small set of cognitive personas, each grounded in a specific psychological theory of humor and a cognitive focus (e.g., Neurotic, Cynic, Observer, Wordsmith, Optimist, Absurdist).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map each persona to a humor theory/mechanism and use them as soft constraints on the reasoning process to ensure candidate pool covers a wide spectrum of comedic mechanisms (Table 1). Example mappings: Neurotic→Relief/Tension Release, Cynic→Superiority/Social Critique, Wordsmith→Linguistic/Ambiguity, Absurdist→Incongruity/Surrealism. Monitor per-persona win rates and adjust persona design if some styles underperform or overfit (paper notes Neurotic and Absurdist dominated; Wordsmith often penalized when forced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Divergent reasoning via Mixture-of-Thought (MoT)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generate K distinct reasoning traces in parallel (instead of a single Chain-of-Thought) to explore multiple comedic angles before selecting a punchline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seed reasoning paths with different cognitive priors to explore the 'long tail' of creative possibilities and avoid mode collapse toward generic, high-probability continuations. MoT should produce diverse candidate sets reflecting irony, absurdity, wordplay, observational humor, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generate many persona-conditioned candidates per prompt
rubrics_metrics.description: For each input prompt, synthesize a large candidate pool covering personas and intra-persona variations (example: 24 candidates per prompt: 4 per persona × 6 personas).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High candidate multiplicity exposes the model to a broad quality spectrum and provides material for pairwise/group ranking and preference learning. The paper used ∼28,800 candidates for 1,200 prompts (24 per prompt).

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Teacher protocol: rank candidates using LLM-judged pairwise evaluation (Elo)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an LLM judge to perform pairwise comparisons across candidates, aggregate match outcomes into a contest matrix, and fit a Bradley–Terry (BT) model to estimate latent Elo-style ratings for each candidate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presentation order should be randomized per match to mitigate position bias. Use an LLM judge (paper used Llama 3.3-70B-Instruct) to compute Elo ratings, then select winners/top candidates for training. Report confidence intervals (paper bootstrapped 95% CIs with 100 bootstrap samples) and statistical significance (non-overlapping CIs).

rubrics_metrics.name: SFT data construction: select multiple top-ranked candidates to avoid mode collapse
rubrics_metrics.description: When building supervised fine-tuning data, select a set of top Elo-ranked candidates per prompt (paper: top 10) rather than a single best example.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including multiple top-ranked candidates per prompt avoids collapsing the student to a single dominant style and teaches a diverse range of humor styles (wordplay, absurdity, sarcasm). In the paper SFT dataset DSFT had N=12,000 (top 10 × 1,200 prompts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) training from pairwise gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct pairwise preference pairs (chosen yw vs. rejected yl) from ranked candidates and optimize the policy directly via DPO without a reward model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create sharp-quality-gap pairs (paper: for each prompt, 5 pairs by randomly pairing top-5 with bottom-5 candidates → 6,000 pairs). Use the DPO objective (provided in paper) with a suitable β hyperparameter. Note: in this study DPO achieved similar performance to SFT, suggesting limited additional benefit when SFT data is high quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offline Group Relative Policy Optimization (O-GRPO) formulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an offline group-relative objective by forming fixed 'Gold Groups' of candidates per prompt (G candidates), computing normalized group-relative advantages from Elo scores, and learning with advantage-weighted losses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute advantage Ai = (ri − µ_group) / (σ_group + ϵ), derive weights wi via softmax temperature T (wi ∝ exp(Ai/T)), and use an exponentially-weighted SFT objective: LO-GRPO(θ) = − E_x [ Σ_i w_i log π_θ(y_i|x) ]. Paper used G=24 and found O-GRPO provided no improvement over high-quality SFT in this domain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cognitive Synergy Distillation (CSD) — include teacher reasoning traces carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Train the student on the teacher's persona-specific reasoning traces alongside the final jokes (<think> …</think> joke) so the student learns both content and planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use symmetric reasoning format for chosen and rejected responses in preference training to avoid shortcuts (so model cannot learn presence of reasoning correlates with winning). However, be cautious: the paper observed an 'explainer trap' where Think/CSD variants underperformed non-Think variants because distilled reasoning biased the model to explain rather than deliver the joke; distill reasoning only when it demonstrably improves generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomized, blinded pairwise evaluation with human validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate model outputs with pairwise comparisons, anonymize model identities, randomize presentation order, and validate a subset with blinded human evaluators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mitigate position and identity bias by anonymization and random swapping. Report inter-annotator agreement, LLM–human consensus, and micro-average correlations. The paper used 50-prompt automated evaluation and 60 human-curated pairwise comparisons (3 evaluators, 180 votes) with blinding and randomization; human agreement was low (31.7%) reflecting humor subjectivity. Use blinding and randomization as standard practice in subjective tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical aggregation: Bradley–Terry model, Elo-scale ratings, and bootstrap CIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregate pairwise match outcomes into a full contest matrix and fit a Bradley–Terry model (MM algorithm) to estimate latent ratings; report Elo-scale ratings with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use bootstrapping (paper: 100 samples) to compute CIs and claim statistical significance via non-overlapping intervals. Report head-to-head win-rate matrices and BT ratings for comparisons across models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure and report humor feature prevalence among winners
rubrics_metrics.description: Annotate winning jokes with salient humor features (e.g., Surprise, Absurdity, Wordplay, Incongruity, Narrative, Sarcasm, Irony, Dark humor) and report prevalence to analyze what drives judged funniness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify co-occurrence and prevalence (paper: Surprise 80%, Absurdity 74.8%, Wordplay 51.3%, etc.) to support claims about dominant mechanisms (expectation violation drives funniness). Use feature analysis to guide persona design and data curation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Watch for and mitigate documented failure modes
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and prevent common failure patterns: (1) generic punchlines defaulting to safe, high-probability completions, (2) overextended setups that bury the punchline, and (3) the 'explainer trap' where reasoning traces cause models to explain rather than deliver jokes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address (1) via persona diversity and forcing low-probability, high-variance generation; (2) by constraining setup length and encouraging punchline brevity; (3) by ablation testing CSD/Think variants and preferring non-Think outputs if reasoning reduces punchiness. Provide concrete examples in development to detect these failure modes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer high-quality, diverse SFT data over alignment complexity in subjective domains
rubrics_metrics.description: In highly subjective tasks like humor, carefully curated, persona-diverse supervised fine-tuning data can outperform or match complex preference-alignment algorithms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper's central empirical finding: 'the quality of the underlying cognitive data (Cognitive Synergy Framework) is the primary driver of generation performance' — DPO matched SFT, O-GRPO underperformed. Prioritize diverse, high-quality SFT data before investing heavily in alignment stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use group and pair construction choices intentionally (sizes, sampling strategies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Design the sizes and sampling strategies of groups and pairings to control signal/noise and learning dynamics (e.g., choose G, number of pairs per prompt, top/bottom bands).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper choices: G=24 (all candidates), DPO pairs: 5 pairs per prompt by pairing top-5 with bottom-5; SFT: top-10 selected. These settings shape the sharpness of preference signals and the diversity preserved for SFT. Tune these hyperparameters with ablations and monitor training stability (early stopping, patience).

rubrics_metrics.name: Training best practices and hyperparameters for reproducible fine-tuning
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply controlled training setups (LoRA adapters, learning rates, batch sizes, sequence lengths, early stopping) and document them for reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper details: LoRA (r=16), SFT LR=2e-4 (linear), SFT epochs=3, DPO/O-GRPO epochs=5 with early stopping (patience=2), batch size global 16, max seq length 1024, bf16 precision. Report runtime and convergence behavior; use consistent settings across Think/non-Think ablations to isolate effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation fairness: hold out an evaluation set entirely
rubrics_metrics.description: Reserve an official held-out evaluation set that is never used during training or data synthesis for final testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper held out SemEval 300-prompt evaluation set for final testing and used a 50-prompt subset for automated pairwise evaluation. Keep evaluation sets fully held-out to avoid leakage from synthetic training data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics and scope disclosure for humor generation
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly acknowledge risks of offensive content, dataset provenance, evaluator recruitment, and domain limitations (language/cultural coverage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer creative mechanisms (wordplay, absurdity) over denigration; disclose that training data derived from public news headlines; report volunteer unpaid human evaluation and limitations (English-only SemEval 2026). Plan multilingual and culturally localized evaluation for future work.
